newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria sale seen in doubt this yr.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria sale seen in doubt this yr.

text.p: Austria is unlikely to achieve its target of floating its entire 17 percent of Bank Austria shares on the Vienna stock exchange this year, a financier involved in the privatisation was quoted as saying on Saturday.
"I do not believe that this enormous transaction can be best placed this year," post office and telecom holding company (PTBG) chief told Die Presse newspaper.

The Austrian government has placed its 17 percent of Bank Austria shares with PTBG in readiness for privatisation. The coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party has pledged to off-load the shares before the end of the year.
"When we took on the shares we signed a contract that we would seek the best possible price. That has to take precedence over the coalition agreement," Becker said.

A planned three billion schillings capital increase by Bank Austria in June, the exchange of Bank Austria shares for shares in recently acquired Creditanstalt and a likely autumn capital increase by Die Erste savings bank would all weigh on the Vienna market, Becker said.

Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger will take the final decision on the Bank Austria sale. No one at the finance ministry was immediately available for comment. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
